test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Sept, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A and B entered a partnership for 5 years. At the start of the business, they invested Rs. 36,000 and Rs. 58,000, respectively. At the end of 5 years, their total profit was Rs. 94,000. What will be the share of B (in Rs.) out of this profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since time period is same (5 years), Profit Ratio = Investment Ratio.

Ratio of A : B = 36,000 : 58,000 = 18 : 29.

Total units = 18 + 29 = 47 units.

47 units = ₹94,000 → 1 unit = ₹2,000.

B's share = 29 units = 29 × 2,000 = ₹58,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹58,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment of A = ₹36,000

Investment of B = ₹58,000

Time period = 5 years

Total Profit = ₹94,000

**Formula Used:**

Profit Share Ratio = (InvestmentA × TimeA) : (InvestmentB × TimeB)

 
 A: ₹36,000
 18 units
 
 B: ₹58,000
 29 units
 
• 
 Total Ratio: 47
 Profit: ₹94k

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit Ratio A : B = (36000 × 5) : (58000 × 5)

⇒ Profit Ratio A : B = 36 : 58 = 18 : 29

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 18 + 29 = 47

⇒ Total Profit = ₹94,000

⇒ B's Share = (29 ÷ 47) × 94,000

⇒ B's Share = 29 × 2,000

⇒ B's Share = ₹58,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹58,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Partnership Law

Profit is always distributed in the ratio of the product of capital and the time for which it was invested (P = C × T).

Case of Equal Time

When the time period for all partners is identical, the profit sharing ratio is exactly the same as the investment ratio (P₁ : P₂ = C₁ : C₂).

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and may receive a fixed salary or commission before the remaining profit is divided according to investment ratios.
